## Loading Packages

```{r}
#| message: true
#| warning: true
library(dslabs)
library(dplyr)
```


# Practice Space


## Single grouping
```{r}
#| eval: false
#| message: true
#| warning: true
#| include: false
# Pre-check
data(stars)
?stars
colnames(stars)
unique(stars$type)
```
**🗣:** Column `type` is the grouping variable, while `magnitude` and `temp` are numeric summary variables.

**🎯:** Calculate the `mean_temperature` and `mean_magnitude` for each star `type` using the `group_by()` and `summarize()` functions.
```{r}
# Code
twinkle_twinkle <- stars %>%
  group_by(type) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_temperature = mean(temp),
    mean_magnitude = mean(magnitude),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```
```{r}
# Check
twinkle_twinkle
is_grouped_df(twinkle_twinkle)
```

**🗣:** The **check** shows one row for each star type: `A`, `B`, `DA`, `DB`, `DF`, `F`, `G`, `K`, `M`, and `O`. The `mean_temperature` column shows the average temperature of each star type; similarly, the `mean_magnitude` shows the average magnitude (i.e., illuminance) of each star type.


## Single grouping + three statistics
```{r}
#| eval: false
#| message: true
#| warning: true
#| include: false
# Pre-check
data(olive)
?olive
colnames(olive)
unique(olive$region)
```
**🗣:** I will use the `eicosenoic` fatty acid variable with the `region` column as the grouping variable.

**🎯:** Calculate the `mean()`, `sd()`, and `n()` of the `eicosenoic` column by `region`.
```{r}
# Pre-code variable
fatty_acid <- "eicosenoic"

# Code
Olive_Garden <- olive %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_value = mean(.data[[fatty_acid]], na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_value   = sd(.data[[fatty_acid]], na.rm = TRUE),
    n          = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```
```{r}
# Check
Olive_Garden
arrange(Olive_Garden, desc(mean_value))
is_grouped_df(Olive_Garden)
```
**🗣:** Southern Italy has the highest `mean_value` of `{r} fatty_acid`. The `n` column shows the number of rows in each region: Northern Italy (151), Sardinia (98), and Southern Italy (323).


## Counting unique values
```{r}
#| eval: false
#| message: true
#| warning: true
#| include: false
# Pre-check
data("us_contagious_diseases")
?us_contagious_diseases
colnames(us_contagious_diseases)
```
```{r}
# Check unique diseases
unique(us_contagious_diseases$disease)

# Determine the number of unique diseases
length(unique(us_contagious_diseases$disease))
```

**🗣:** There are `{r} length(unique(us_contagious_diseases$disease))` unique diseases within the `disease` column of the `us_contagious_diseases` dataset. They are `{r} paste(unique(us_contagious_diseases$disease), collapse = ", ")`.

```{r}
# Check unique states
unique(us_contagious_diseases$state)

# Determine the number of unique states
length(unique(us_contagious_diseases$state))
```
**🗣:** There are `{r} length(unique(us_contagious_diseases$state))` distinct values within the `state` column of the `us_contagious_diseases` dataset.


## Make and test a prediction
**🎯:** Group `us_contagious_diseases` by both `state` and `disease` and report the number of groups created.

**🐱:** There are `{r} length(unique(us_contagious_diseases$state))` states and `{r} length(unique(us_contagious_diseases$disease))` diseases, so the tibble created will likely include `51 x 7 = 357` groups.

```{r}
# Code
categorical_counts <- us_contagious_diseases %>%
  group_by(state, disease) %>%
  count()
```
```{r}
# Check
categorical_counts
count(categorical_counts)
```
**🗣:** The `categorical_counts` includes 357 rows, which is congruent with the predicted `51 x 7 = 357` count.


## Mean reported counts by diseases
**🎯:** Using the `us_contagious_diseases` dataset, create a summary column named `national_mean_count` that calculates the mean of `count` across `state` and `year` for each `disease`. Save only the three diseases with the highest values in that column in a data.frame named `Infectious_Burden`.

```{r}
# Code
Infectious_Burden <- us_contagious_diseases %>%
  group_by(disease) %>%
  summarize(
    national_mean_count = mean(count, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(national_mean_count)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 3)
```
```{r}
# Check
Infectious_Burden
nrow(Infectious_Burden)
is_grouped_df(Infectious_Burden)
```
**🗣:** The `Infectious_Burden` data.frame includes data for `{r} paste(unique(Infectious_Burden$disease), collapse = ", ")`. The tibble is classified as `3 x 2`, with only two columns, `disease` and `national_mean_count`.


## Final reflection
**📝:** The function `group_by()` sorts the data.frame by the specified variables (e.g., region, disease, state, so on). Afterwards, the `summarize()` function can be used create the specified summaries for those specific variables. This function is also useful for creating new summary columns (e.g., `national_mean_count`), whereas `count()` can be used to simply create frequency tables for an entire dataset.
